prior_year_events.event_name: Lloyd's Part VII Transfer to Lloyd's Brussels
prior_year_events.impact_description: Transfer of relevant policies to Lloyd's Insurance Company S.A. (Lloyd's Brussels) with a 100% quota share reinsurance back to the Syndicate; transferred funds reported as deposits with ceding undertakings and affected the treatment and presentation of EEA risks and related reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding increased by GBP 383.949m during 2021 (a 29.6% increase on the opening gross reserve of GBP 1,297.112m). The movement represents an adverse prior-year development (strengthening) primarily associated with adverse claims development across the reinsurance portfolio and changes in reinsurance recoveries; the Part VII transfer of EEA policies to Lloyd's Brussels and related reinsurance arrangements are noted in the report and have affected presentation and flows of reinsurance and deposits.
raw_causal_phrases: On 30 December 2020, the Members and former Members of the Syndicate, as comprised for each of the relevant years of account between 1993 and April 2019 (or October 2020 in the case of German reinsurance), transferred all relevant policies (and related liabilities) underwritten by them for those years of account to Lloyd's Insurance Company S.A. ('Lloyd's Brussels'), in accordance with Part VII of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
Following the Part VII Transfer, the Syndicate transferred funds to Lloyd's Insurance Company S.A. ("Lloyd's Brussels") and these funds are to be utilised to settle all EEA claims.
Negative movements on claims incurred net of reinsurance arose in respect of the following classes of business:

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development used is the GROSS 'Change in prior year provisions' line from Note 17 (gross GBP 383,949k). Some other notes (e.g. Note 6 and P&L lines) report related net movements and claims-incurred figures - these were avoided per instructions. The Part VII RITC / Lloyd's Brussels transfers are present in the report and may distort comparatives and triangles. Several class movements available in the notes are presented net of reinsurance; lob_movements entries other than the gross reinsurance strengthening are therefore lower-confidence net figures.
